abstract: How does local cortical physiology shape interactions between brain regions? We combined neural mass modelling with human and macaque intracranial recordings to examine how synaptic kinetics link oscillatory waveform morphology to cortical interactions. In a modified excitatory-inhibitory Wilson-Cowan model, synaptic rise and decay kinetics shaped waveform geometry and phase-dependent responsiveness. Local kinetics and coupling symmetry jointly influenced interaction measures and temporal irreversibility, while phase-locked perturbations altered imaginary coherency and bivariate irreversibility even when the coupling strengths remained fixed. In stereo-EEG from 23 patients, waveform asymmetry was most strongly associated with local irreversibility, whereas mean instantaneous alpha frequency showed stronger associations with interregional measures. Subdural macaque electrocorticography reproduced the frequency associations but not the local waveform association. Together, these findings show that waveform shape carries information about local neuronal dynamics, provide a mechanistic framework for interpreting cortical interactions, and motivate testing waveform morphology as a guide to stimulation timing.
